The sum \(S_r = \sum_{m \geq 0} \binom{10000}{502m + r}\) is the sum of binomial coefficients \(\binom{10000}{k}\) for \(0 \leq k \leq 10000\) and \(k \equiv r \pmod{502}\), with \(\binom{10000}{k} = 0\) for \(k > 10000\). The goal is to determine how many of \(S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_{501}\) are divisible by the prime 503.

Using the roots of unity filter and working in the field \(\mathbb{Z}/503\mathbb{Z}\), \(S_r \equiv 502 f(r) \pmod{503}\) where \(f(r) = \sum_{\zeta} \zeta^{-r} (1 + \zeta)^{10000}\), and \(\zeta\) runs over the 502nd roots of unity in the field. Since the multiplicative group of \(\mathbb{Z}/503\mathbb{Z}\) has order 502, a primitive 502nd root of unity exists. Note that \(502 \equiv -1 \pmod{503}\), and the inverse of 502 modulo 503 is 502, so \(S_r \equiv -f(r) \pmod{503}\). Thus, \(S_r \equiv 0 \pmod{503}\) if and only if \(f(r) \equiv 0 \pmod{503}\).

The term \((1 + \zeta)^{10000}\) depends only on the exponent modulo the order of the multiplicative group, which is 502. Compute \(10000 \mod 502\):
\[
10000 = 502 \times 19 + 462, \quad \text{so} \quad 10000 \equiv 462 \pmod{502}.
\]
For all \(\zeta\) (including when \(1 + \zeta = 0\), since \(10000 > 0\) and \(462 > 0\)), \((1 + \zeta)^{10000} \equiv (1 + \zeta)^{462} \pmod{503}\). Thus,
\[
f(r) \equiv \sum_{\zeta} \zeta^{-r} (1 + \zeta)^{462} \pmod{503}.
\]

The polynomial \(g(x) = (1 + x)^{462}\) has degree 462. Since \(462 < 502\), using the roots of unity filter, the sum \(\sum_{\zeta} \zeta^{-r} g(\zeta)\) equals 502 times the coefficient of \(x^r\) in \(g(x)\), which is \(\binom{462}{r}\), and is zero for \(r\) not in \(\{0, 1, \ldots, 462\}\). Specifically,
\[
f(r) \equiv
\begin{cases}
502 \binom{462}{r} \pmod{503} & \text{if } 0 \leq r \leq 462, \\
0 & \text{if } r > 462.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(502 \equiv -1 \pmod{503}\),
\[
f(r) \equiv
\begin{cases}
-\binom{462}{r} \pmod{503} & \text{if } 0 \leq r \leq 462, \\
0 & \text{if } r > 462.
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
S_r \equiv -f(r) \equiv
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r} \pmod{503} & \text{if } 0 \leq r \leq 462, \\
0 & \text{if } r > 462.
\end{cases}
\]

Now, \(S_r \equiv 0 \pmod{503}\) if either:
- \(r > 462\) and \(S_r \equiv 0\) (which holds), or
- \(0 \leq r \leq 462\) and \(\binom{462}{r} \equiv 0 \pmod{503}\).

However, since \(503 > 462\), and 503 is prime, \(\binom{462}{r}\) is not divisible by 503 for any \(r\) in \(\{0, 1, \ldots, 462\}\). Thus, \(S_r \equiv \binom{462}{r} \not\equiv 0 \pmod{503}\) for \(r = 0, 1, \ldots, 462\).

Therefore, \(S_r \equiv 0 \pmod{503}\) only for \(r > 462\). Since \(r < 502\), the possible \(r\) are the integers from 463 to 501 inclusive. The number of such \(r\) is:
\[
501 - 463 + 1 = 39.
\]

The values of \(r\) from 0 to 501 include 502 terms. The number of \(r \leq 462\) is 463 (from 0 to 462 inclusive), so the number of \(r > 462\) is \(502 - 463 = 39\).

Thus, there are 39 values of \(r\) for which \(S_r\) is divisible by 503.
